product_overview: SafeNap is a browser-based drowsiness detection dashboard that monitors the user's face in real time, calculates fatigue indicators, and triggers visual, audio, and vibration alerts when sleepiness is detected. It also supports optional Arduino-connected alarm hardware and multi-device session synchronization.
core_goals: Start and stop camera-based drowsiness monitoring from the browser
Calibrate eye-closure detection to create a personalized fatigue threshold
View real-time drowsiness metrics and session statistics
Receive and acknowledge fatigue alerts when drowsiness is detected
Connect and test Arduino alarm hardware from the app
Monitor model status and train the optional on-browser ML drowsiness model
See backend connection and multi-device monitoring status

features.name: Camera Monitoring Start/Stop
features.description: Lets the user begin or end webcam-based drowsiness monitoring, including camera permission, detector-role assignment, and automatic calibration launch.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Wait for the camera control to become available -> Start monitoring -> Approve camera permission -> See the monitoring view become active and the calibration wizard open
Navigate to / -> Start monitoring -> Observe the status change to indicate active face monitoring or no face detected -> Stop monitoring -> See the camera return to inactive state
Navigate to / -> Start monitoring while another device is already controlling detection -> Observe the notice that this device became a viewer instead of the detector
Navigate to / -> Start monitoring -> Switch away from the tab -> Observe the camera stop automatically when the page is hidden

features.name: Calibration Wizard
features.description: Guides the user through a two-step eye-open and eye-closed calibration process to compute a personalized detection threshold, with options to skip, retry, or reuse an older calibration.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Start the camera -> See the calibration wizard appear -> Begin calibration -> Keep eyes open during the first phase -> Keep eyes closed during the second phase -> See the success result with threshold values -> Start monitoring
Navigate to / -> Start the camera -> See the calibration wizard appear -> Skip calibration -> Continue using the default detection threshold
Navigate to / -> Start the camera -> Begin calibration -> Encounter a calibration failure due to the user's calibration attempt -> Retry calibration -> Complete the phases successfully
Navigate to / -> Start the camera after an older calibration exists -> See the recalibration prompt -> Choose to keep the current calibration -> Continue into monitoring

features.name: Calibration Panel Controls
features.description: Provides controls to trigger recalibration, clear stored calibration, and switch the detection sensitivity preset.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Start the camera -> Open the calibration panel -> Trigger calibration from the panel -> Complete calibration and return to monitoring
Navigate to / -> Open the calibration panel -> Clear the stored calibration -> Observe that the calibration data is removed
Navigate to / -> Open the calibration panel -> Switch between Leve, Padrão, and Alta sensitivity presets -> Observe the active preset change

features.name: Arduino Connection
features.description: Allows the user to connect the app to an Arduino Nano alarm device through the backend serial manager.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Enter an optional serial port such as COM3 -> Connect to the Arduino -> See the connection success message
Navigate to / -> Leave the port empty or enter a port value -> Connect to the Arduino -> See the connection result message

features.name: Hardware Test Commands
features.description: Lets the user send test commands to the connected Arduino alarm hardware for sound, vibration, or stop output.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Connect to the Arduino -> Trigger the alarm test command -> Observe the hardware alarm test output
Navigate to / -> Connect to the Arduino -> Trigger the vibration test command -> Observe the vibration test output
Navigate to / -> Connect to the Arduino -> Trigger the stop-output command -> Observe the hardware output stop

features.name: Drowsiness Alert Overlay with Acknowledge
features.description: Shows a fullscreen warning or alarm overlay when the system detects drowsiness, and lets the user acknowledge the alarm once awake.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Start monitoring -> Trigger a drowsiness condition -> See the warning or alarm overlay appear automatically
Navigate to / -> Start monitoring -> Trigger a drowsiness alarm -> Acknowledge the alert by confirming you are awake -> Return to normal monitoring

features.name: Live Metrics Display
features.description: Shows the user real-time fatigue metrics, charts, and session statistics while monitoring is active.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Start monitoring -> View the PERCLOS gauge and safety state -> View the live EAR and PERCLOS chart updating over time -> View session statistics updating in real time

features.name: ML Model Status and Training
features.description: Displays the on-browser ML model state, collected sample counts, and training controls for the optional drowsiness model.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> View the ML model status and drowsiness score -> View collected sample progress for alert and sleepy classes
Navigate to / -> Collect enough labeled samples -> Start training or retraining the model -> See the model status update after training
Navigate to / -> Open the ML training panel -> Clear the collected training data -> Observe the sample counts reset

features.name: Backend Connection Status
features.description: Shows whether the app is connected to the backend WebSocket and displays the current safety state in the header.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> View the backend connection badge -> Observe whether the app is Online or Offline -> View the current safety state badge in the header

tech_stack: WebSocket client (realtime sync with FastAPI backend)

routes.description: Single-page dashboard with camera monitoring, drowsiness gauge, live charts, session stats, calibration, hardware controls and ML status cards

features.name: Camera Monitoring Start/Stop
features.description: Start or stop the webcam-based drowsiness monitoring. On start the app claims the detector role (multi-device), requests camera permission, loads the MediaPipe face model and opens the calibration wizard.
user_interactions: Click "Iniciar" button to start the camera (browser permission prompt appears)
Observe status badge change from Inativo to Monitorando/Sem rosto
Observe FPS counter and EAR bar while camera is active
Click "Parar" button to stop the camera
If another device already holds the detector role, a yellow notice "Outro dispositivo já está monitorando. Este virou espectador." is shown

features.name: Calibration Wizard
features.description: Guided 2-phase calibration (eyes open, then eyes closed) shown automatically when the camera starts. Can be skipped or re-run. Computes a personalized EAR threshold.
user_interactions: On wizard intro screen, click "Começar" to start calibration
Keep eyes open during phase 1 until progress bar completes
Keep eyes closed during phase 2 until progress bar completes
See success screen with threshold values and click "Iniciar monitoramento"
Or click "Pular" to skip calibration and use defaults
On failure, click "Tentar" to retry

features.name: Calibration Panel Controls
features.description: Sidebar panel to recalibrate, clear calibration and choose detection sensitivity preset (Leve/Padrão/Alta).
user_interactions: Click "Calibrar" button (enabled only when camera is active)
Click trash icon to clear stored calibration
Click sensitivity preset buttons (Leve, Padrão, Alta)

features.name: Arduino Connection
features.description: Connect to the Arduino Nano alarm device through the FastAPI backend serial manager.
user_interactions: Optionally type serial port (e.g. COM3) into the port input
Click "Conectar" button
See success or failure alert message

features.name: Hardware Test Commands
features.description: Send test commands to the Arduino alarm hardware (sound alarm, vibration, off) via backend API.
user_interactions: Click "Alarme" button to trigger sound alarm test
Click "Vibração" button to trigger vibration test
Click "Desligar" button to stop alert output

features.name: Drowsiness Alert Overlay with Acknowledge
features.description: Fullscreen alarm overlay with sound and vibration when drowsiness is detected (PERCLOS, eyes closed, yawn, head drop). User acknowledges by clicking the alarm button.
user_interactions: Observe warning or alarm overlay appear automatically when drowsiness detected
Click "Estou acordado" button to acknowledge the alarm

features.name: Live Metrics Display
features.description: Realtime PERCLOS gauge, EAR/PERCLOS 60-second chart and session statistics (active time, blink count, average EAR, warning count).
user_interactions: View PERCLOS gauge and state badge (Normal/Atenção/Perigo)
View live EAR/PERCLOS chart updating every second
View session statistics updating in realtime

features.name: ML Model Status and Training
features.description: Displays on-browser ML model status and drowsiness score; collects labeled samples and allows manual model training with minimum 50 samples per class.
user_interactions: View ML model status badge and drowsiness score percentage
View collected sample counts (Alertas/Sonolento) and progress bar
Click "Treinar" or "Re-treinar" button when enough samples exist
Click trash icon to clear collected training data

features.name: Backend Connection Status
features.description: Header badges showing safety state and WebSocket connection status to the backend.
user_interactions: View Online/Offline badge and Normal/Atenção/Perigo state in header

known_limitations.issue: Camera start requires browser camera permission; automated tests cannot exercise real video detection without a fake video device
known_limitations.impact: Drowsiness detection, calibration and alert overlay flows depend on a live camera stream

known_limitations.issue: Backend FastAPI (port 8000) must be running for Arduino/hardware endpoints and WebSocket; otherwise WS badge shows Offline and hardware calls fail
known_limitations.impact: Hardware connect/test and multi-device sync features depend on backend availability

known_limitations.issue: MediaPipe WASM model loads from CDN at runtime; may fail offline, degrading to video-only mode
known_limitations.impact: Detection disabled when model load fails (warning badge shown)
